actions.action: Buy 1/2 in CPVC pipe and fittings (elbows/tees) from a hardware store
Cut CPVC into sections (about 4 in, 3.5 in and 7 in) sized to the pot
Glue the pieces into a T or zig-zag stake holder, using a level to keep the stake section vertical
Drill holes in the pot bottom and zip-tie the support in place, then trim the ties
Add base material (gravel/rock) to the bottom of the pot
Remove the plant from its old pot and work loose the rootbound roots
Replant the plant with its stake slid into the anchored support

verdict.reason: The video addresses climbing plants falling over by anchoring a stake, not a top-heavy unstable pot, so the diagnosis is only partial; the PVC stake anchor would not counterbalance the pot like nesting it in a larger pot, though it isn't likely to harm the orchid.
